title: Minor/expository: tighten well-definedness of φ in Lemma 2 (lem:rho-surj)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location.** solution.tex Lemma 2 (lem:rho-surj), the paragraph beginning "This is well defined:".

The well-definedness of $\varphi\in\operatorname{Hom}_A(I/I^2,A)$ is load-bearing (it is what makes $\rho$ surjective), and the current write-up is correct but logically muddled. The clean statement: since the chosen $f_1,\dots,f_r$ reduce to a **$k$-basis** of $V=I/\mathfrak m_R I$, any $A$-linear relation $\sum_j a_j[f_j]=0$ in $I/I^2$ lifts to $\sum_j\tilde a_j f_j\in I^2\subseteq\mathfrak m_R I$; reducing mod $\mathfrak m_R$ gives $\sum_j\bar a_j(f_j\bmod\mathfrak m_R I)=0$ in $V$, and because the $f_j\bmod\mathfrak m_R I$ are a **basis**, *every* $\bar a_j=0$, i.e. each $a_j\in\mathfrak m$. Since $\varphi([f_j])\in k\cdot 1_A$ is annihilated by $\mathfrak m$, $a_j\varphi([f_j])=0$ and the relation is preserved.

**How to close.** Replace the existing paragraph with the above. This is a clarity fix, not a true error; flagged because the step is essential and the present phrasing obscures that all coefficients (not merely a particular linear combination) vanish.
